title: billing.customer.created payload
description: The `data` payload of the `billing.customer.created` event: billing's own customer row now exists for one of identity's entities. `owner` is a reference across a service boundary — identity's uuid, stored as a uuid, with no foreign key and nothing to join on inside this process — so it is the one field a consumer cannot do without. The envelope is validated by schemas/event-envelope.schema.json; this schema validates what is inside `data`. The file path is the event type with dots as directory separators. See docs/event-naming.md.

id.description: billing's customer row. Always equal to the envelope's `subject`. A billing id, not a cafaye-prefixed one — billing's primary keys are uuids and `sub_…`/`pln_…` are the subscription and plan, not this.

owner.description: The identity-side entity this customer bills. Present because without it the customer cannot be charged: there is no other field on the payload that names who pays.

type.description: Which kind of identity entity. A closed set of two, because it is a constant in the publisher rather than a free-form string, and a closed set is what lets a consumer switch on it.

id.description: identity's id for that entity, as a bare uuid — the same value `identity.*`'s `user_id` carries, and it joins. This repository once said otherwise about identity's events and the two schemas disagreed; see D7, whose second half was false, and D35 for the correction.

processor.description: The payment processor this customer lives at. An owner may legitimately have a customer at two processors, so it is part of the uniqueness rule and cannot be inferred.

processor_customer_id.description: The processor's own id for this customer, or null before the first processor call. Nullable on purpose: v0 stores the name only, and a consumer that treats null as an error will break the day a real customer is created.

email.description: The address on file, or null. Billing does not own the person; this is a copy that may be stale.

metadata.description: Free-form attributes the caller attached, or the empty object. **The one place this schema is deliberately open**, because it is an open bag by design: closing it would make the field useless, and a field with no declared keys is not a field core can say anything about. Everything else here is closed, and everything here is a fact about money.

created_at.description: RFC3339 UTC when the row was written.

updated_at.description: RFC3339 UTC when the row last changed. There is no `billing.customer.updated` in the catalog, so today this is always equal to `created_at`.
